summary: In May 2026 Indian authorities cancelled NEET results and ordered a re-examination after allegations that question papers had leaked before the test, a reversal that hit candidates who believed they had already secured their places. Reports of at least 13 student suicides in the surrounding weeks sharpened public anger. The response began online as political satire — the name Cockroach Janta Party reclaims a remark attributed to a Chief Justice comparing unemployed youth to cockroaches — and hardened into an organised campaign demanding the education minister's resignation and structural reform of the national examination system. Demonstrations centred on Jantar Mantar in Delhi until police cleared the camp in mid-July, and a march on Parliament on 20 July ended in tear gas and baton charges.

faq.q: What is the Cockroach Janta Party?
faq.a: It is a protest movement rather than a registered political party. The name is used as a rallying identity, reclaiming a remark attributed to a Chief Justice that compared unemployed youth to cockroaches. The campaign began as memes and posts on social media in May 2026 and grew into organised demonstrations.

faq.q: Why were the 2026 NEET results cancelled?
faq.a: Authorities cancelled the results and ordered a re-examination in May 2026 after allegations that question papers had leaked before the test. NEET is India's single largest gateway to undergraduate medical education, so the reversal affected candidates who believed they had already secured places, and coverage framed it as the latest in a series of examination controversies.

Two things: the resignation of the education minister, and structural reform of the national examination system — stronger safeguards against paper leaks and clearer accountability when results are challenged. Supporters describe these as practical fixes rather than partisan goals, and the campaign has drawn participants from across political affiliations.

faq.q: What happened at the march on Parliament?
faq.a: On 20 July 2026 more than 10,000 people marched toward Parliament. Police responded with tear gas and batons; around 180 people were reported injured and 70 detained. It followed the clearing of the Jantar Mantar protest camp in mid-July and the forcible removal of hunger-striking activist Sonam Wangchuk to hospital.

faq.q: How does the exam scandal connect to unemployment?
faq.a: Graduate youth unemployment in India has been reported above 15 percent, leaving many educated young people frustrated by limited opportunities. For many participants the exam scandal became a symbol of wider grievances about fairness, mobility and the gap between qualifications earned and jobs available.

Organisers paused street marches after 21 July 2026 over safety concerns while vowing to continue the protest, and demonstrators rebuilt the demolished camp. The status badge at the top of this page and the coverage chart reflect whether new reporting is still arriving, so they are the current answer rather than this note.
